concept: The whole day turns on one number, so the hero greys out the good part (New Zealand 70 for 5) and puts the twist in bright white: India never took a sixth wicket. Slide 2 is the collapse as a bar chart, one bar per wicket showing NZ's score when it fell, so the five short bars and then the long tea bar make the fightback visible before you read a word. Slide 3 gives the Nicholls and Phillips stand one giant number, and slide 4 lists the small things that let the day slip before asking what India do on day 2. Cricket blue, type and data only: no player photos, no logos.
caption:
New Zealand were 70 for 5. India didn't take another wicket.

Shubman Gill won the toss and bowled first on a grassy Basin Reserve pitch. It worked. Jasprit Bumrah bowled Tom Latham in the first over and finished the morning burst with three wickets. Anshul Kamboj and Akash Deep took one each.

Then Henry Nicholls and Glenn Phillips batted through the rest of day 1. Their unbroken 6th-wicket stand went past 100 and Nicholls reached his hundred in the final session.

India had their chances. Rachin Ravindra edged one behind that India didn't review and they lost a review against Phillips. Mohammed Siraj and Ravindra Jadeja were left out of the XI.

Can India's bowlers get it back on day 2? Tell us below.
